verdict.rationale: Clerk documents its own machine authentication: M2M tokens that authenticate calls between agents, and API keys that authenticate programmatic callers as a Clerk user or org. It also ships per-tool-call gating against the caller's Clerk permissions and scopes, plus custom OAuth scopes for MCP clients. This gives agents distinct, scoped credentials instead of a shared human login, but the evidence never shows how M2M tokens or API keys are revoked, nor how narrowly their scopes can be set. The documented revocation covers human sessions only. missing for 10: documented instant revocation of M2M tokens/API keys, detail on per-agent least-privilege scoping for machine identities, independent or hands-on corroboration.
